href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="remote-control-for-local-agents"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/remote-control-local-agents">Remote control for local agents</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>You can now see and reply to the local agents running on your computer from the Cursor iOS app.</p>
<h2 id="get-started" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#get-started" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Get started</h2>
<p>Remote Control is on by default for everyone except Enterprise organizations.</p>
<p>Download the Cursor iOS app and sign in. Computers on your account appear in the app automatically. Tap your computer in the app and approve your pairing request in the Cursor desktop app. Your local agents appear in a list. Tap one to see what it&#x27;s doing or send it a message.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Remote Control for local agents in the Cursor iOS app" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fremote-control-cl-pezewO3SZRrIQxMNaTzdpsP9TD1ChS.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fremote-control-cl-pezewO3SZRrIQxMNaTzdpsP9TD1ChS.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fremote-control-cl-pezewO3SZRrIQxMNaTzdpsP9TD1ChS.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="agents-keep-running-on-your-computer" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#agents-keep-running-on-your-computer" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Agents keep running on your computer</h2>
<p>Remote control doesn&#x27;t move your agents anywhere. It keeps running on your computer, and the app connects to it. Your computer needs to stay on and online for remote control to work.</p>
<h2 id="keep-your-computer-awake" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#keep-your-computer-awake" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Keep your computer awake</h2>
<p>To stop your computer from sleeping while you&#x27;re away, turn on &quot;Keep this computer awake&quot; under Remote Control in Cursor&#x27;s desktop settings. Your computer needs to be plugged in with the lid open.</p>
<h2 id="for-enterprise-teams" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#for-enterprise-teams" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>For Enterprise teams</h2>
<p>Remote control is on by default, except for Enterprise organizations. Enterprise admins can turn it on in Org settings &gt; Security and identity &gt; Remote control.</p>
<p>Remote control doesn&#x27;t require cloud agents to work.</p>
<p>Remote control is available today in the <a href="https://cursor.com/mobile" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cursor iOS app</a>.</p></div></div></div></div></article><article><div class="grid-cursor gap-y-0 pb-v5 mb-v5 border-theme-border-02 border-b"><div class="mb-v2/12 col-span-full max-xl:mx-auto max-xl:w-full max-xl:max-w-[48rem] xl:col-end-7"><p class="text-theme-text-sec sticky top-[var(--site-sticky-top)] left-[-1px] inline-flex items-center"><a class="hover:text-theme-text inline-flex items-center" href="/changelog/rollouts-and-security-reviewer"><time dateTime="2026-09-23T00:00:00.000Z" class="type-base">Sep 23, 2026</time></a><span class="xl:hidden"> · </span><a class="text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text active:text-theme-text xl:hidden" href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="rollouts-and-security-review"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/rollouts-and-security-reviewer">Rollouts and Security Review</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>Today we&#x27;re launching two Cursor bots for the last mile of shipping code. Rollouts watches every change as it deploys and reports its health per environment. Security Review reports exploitable bugs on every pull request.</p>
<p>Both are available today on Teams and Enterprise plans.</p>
<h2 id="rollouts" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#rollouts" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Rollouts</h2>
<p>Rollouts attaches a monitor to every pull request and watches the change as it deploys, reporting change health per environment: verified healthy, regression detected, or inconclusive. It&#x27;s the Cursor version of <a href="https://cursor.com/blog/firetiger" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Firetiger</a> Change Monitors, rebuilt with the Bot Development Kit.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/5Tb5ctSIPf90200no008q8EIiacgKGmFjxrFLk1tAmRmjI/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>Enable it from the dashboard and connect source control, your deploy system, and your telemetry provider. Rollouts starts watching on the next pull request.</p>
<h4 id="monitoring-plans" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#monitoring-plans" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Monitoring plans</h4>
<p>When a pull request opens, Rollouts reads the diff and the systems it touches, then writes a monitoring plan as a PR comment. The plan lists the risks it identified, the effect the change is meant to have, the signals it will check, and any gaps in instrumentation that would make the change hard to verify. Edit the plan in the PR and Rollouts uses your version.</p>
<h4 id="deploy-tracking" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#deploy-tracking" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Deploy tracking</h4>
<p>Rollouts wakes on deploy events for the change&#x27;s commit and runs the plan against your logs, metrics, and traces. It tracks each environment separately, so a change can be verified in staging and still flagged in production. Rollouts checks the change&#x27;s intended effect alongside error and latency signals, and reports back on the PR when it reaches a verdict.</p>
<h4 id="regressions" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#regressions" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Regressions</h4>
<p>When Rollouts detects a regression, it names the change it suspects and notifies the author. Depending on configuration, it can also open a revert PR for review or hand the finding to a cloud agent for a fix. Rollouts does not merge or roll back on its own today.</p>
<h4 id="integrations" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#integrations" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Integrations</h4>
<p>Rollouts connects to Origin or GitHub for source control, to your continuous delivery system for deploy events, and to Datadog and other telemetry providers for signals. Feature flag integration is coming soon.</p>
<h2 id="security-review" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#security-review" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Security Review</h2>
<p>Security Review is available today. It reads every pull request in the context of the codebase and posts one review comment reporting exploitable bugs. Style and quality stay with Bugbot.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Security Review comment on a pull request reporting an exploitable bug with a severity and proposed fix" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fsecurity-review-N8azgyLevr8FvNIRqJN6hk71os2Oxu.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fsecurity-review-N8azgyLevr8FvNIRqJN6hk71os2Oxu.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fsecurity-review-N8azgyLevr8FvNIRqJN6hk71os2Oxu.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<p>Enable it from the dashboard for the repositories you want reviewed. Draft PRs are skipped.</p>
<h4 id="what-it-reports" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#what-it-reports" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>What it reports</h4>
<p>Security Review looks for injection across SQL, command, and template surfaces, along with authentication and authorization bypasses, including checks that a refactor stopped running. It also flags secrets and credentials committed to source, SSRF and unvalidated redirects, unsafe deserialization, and dependency changes that introduce known vulnerabilities. It traces where user input enters and what it passes through.</p>
<h4 id="findings" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#findings" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Findings</h4>
<p>Each finding carries a severity, the attack path, and a proposed fix. Dismiss one with a reason and Security Review won&#x27;t raise it again on that PR.</p>
<h4 id="team-rules" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#team-rules" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Team rules</h4>
<p>Add rules for your codebase, such as which client external calls must go through or which tables are never queried from a request handler, and Security Review enforces them on every PR.</p>
<h2 id="get-started" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#get-started" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Get started</h2>
<p>Rollouts and Security Reviewer are available today on Teams and Enterprise plans. Enable either bot from the <a href="https://cursor.com/automations" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">automations</a> tab.</p>
<p>For the next 10 days, we&#x27;re including usage credits so teams can try Rollouts on real changes. Teams and Enterprise customers receive credits for roughly 50 and 500 changes, respectively.</p></div></div></div></div></article><article><div class="grid-cursor gap-y-0 pb-v5 mb-v5 border-theme-border-02 border-b"><div class="mb-v2/12 col-span-full max-xl:mx-auto max-xl:w-full max-xl:max-w-[48rem] xl:col-end-7"><p class="text-theme-text-sec sticky top-[var(--site-sticky-top)] left-[-1px] inline-flex items-center"><a class="hover:text-theme-text inline-flex items-center" href="/changelog/projects"><time dateTime="2026-09-10T00:00:00.000Z" class="type-base">Sep 10, 2026</time></a><span class="xl:hidden"> · </span><a class="text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text active:text-theme-text xl:hidden" href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="cursor-projects"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/projects">Cursor Projects</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/7PpKLPBRpzltNUsAM2tITF544siux77yeTAtxXaM5zY/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>Today we&#x27;re launching Projects in Cursor. Projects lets you take on larger bodies of work, such as a feature, a migration, or a full app. It maintains context over months of work, delegates tasks to thousands of subagents, and performs recurring work without being prompted.</p>
<p>Access Projects from the left-hand nav. The coordinator agent in a project doesn&#x27;t write code itself; it plans the work, delegates it to agents that implement it, and brings the finished work back to you to check. Coordinators create and manage agents on your behalf, running as many in parallel as the work needs.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/guK4iheYZylsctjoMBOuaqStvXVcqvHC7KfB022wD9g00/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h2 id="powered-by-cloud-agents" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#powered-by-cloud-agents" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Powered by Cloud Agents</h2>
<p>A Project runs on its own computer in the cloud, so closing your laptop doesn&#x27;t stop it. When something needs testing on your machine, the coordinator spins up a local agent to run it there.</p>
<h2 id="shared-context" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#shared-context" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Shared context</h2>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/pVrq015he7aaw7HqmbsMMYrOMMVmhkOZQn01hqLBhHqSE/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>You shouldn&#x27;t have to onboard an agent every time you start a task. Each Project maintains a set of files that sync across every cloud and local machine its agents use. Agents add research and artifacts, along with what they learn about the codebase and how you prefer work to be done. If one agent figures out how to test a service, for example, every future agent can use those instructions. The shared context grows with the Project, making the coordinator more effective over time.</p>
<h2 id="subscriptions" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#subscriptions" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Subscriptions</h2>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/F02pXSeJF6CAeEE39x6AM6EHptkXadTzcHwoJ8yNd88o/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>Tell the coordinator agent to watch a Slack channel, run on a schedule, or follow all your PRs. This way it can take action based on signals it detects, without waiting for your prompt.</p>
<p>Connect Slack and point it at a bug-report channel, and it starts delegating each time a bug comes in.</p>
<p>Projects are available in beta and rolling out to all users starting today.</p></div></div></div></div></article><article><div class="grid-cursor gap-y-0 pb-v5 mb-v5 border-theme-border-02 border-b"><div class="mb-v2/12 col-span-full max-xl:mx-auto max-xl:w-full max-xl:max-w-[48rem] xl:col-end-7"><p class="text-theme-text-sec sticky top-[var(--site-sticky-top)] left-[-1px] inline-flex items-center"><a class="hover:text-theme-text inline-flex items-center" href="/changelog/self-hosted-machines"><time dateTime="2026-09-02T00:00:00.000Z" class="type-base">Sep 2, 2026</time></a><span class="xl:hidden"> · </span><a class="text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text active:text-theme-text xl:hidden" href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="self-hosted-machines"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/self-hosted-machines">Self-hosted machines</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>Cursor supports <strong>self-hosted machines</strong>, which let you keep tool execution entirely in your own network.</p>
<p>Your codebase, build outputs, and secrets all stay on internal machines running in your infrastructure, while the agent handles tool calls locally.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Run on menu showing Remote Machines with self-hosted options lambda-test, cloud-demo, and jacks-desktop" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fremote-machines-QjJ0ZzGDelSdT7v2CXDdh0BQHqjmH0.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fremote-machines-QjJ0ZzGDelSdT7v2CXDdh0BQHqjmH0.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fremote-machines-QjJ0ZzGDelSdT7v2CXDdh0BQHqjmH0.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="dynamic-pool-scheduling" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#dynamic-pool-scheduling" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Dynamic pool scheduling</h2>
<p><strong>My Machines</strong> connects a single laptop or VM to your account for personal workflows.</p>
<p><strong>Team pools</strong> are named queues of workers for a team or enterprise. Capacity can grow as requests arrive and shrink when workers disconnect, so your self-hosted machines can scale with demand. Pools are not tied to one repository: name the pool, and any available worker can claim the request.</p>
<p>Pools can also hibernate idle machines, then restore within a reconnect window when a follow-up arrives, so you don&#x27;t keep expensive capacity warm just for the next prompt.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Cloud Agents dashboard listing Self-hosted Machines pools with active and idle worker counts" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fpools-mNNea8rJyNxaBuz7rSVT2SJOKkRsmv.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fpools-mNNea8rJyNxaBuz7rSVT2SJOKkRsmv.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fpools-mNNea8rJyNxaBuz7rSVT2SJOKkRsmv.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="run-on-your-sandboxes" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#run-on-your-sandboxes" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Run on your sandboxes</h2>
<p>Cloud agents can now execute on <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted/integrations" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">infrastructure you already use</a>, including from AWS Lambda, Coder, Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, Namespace, Vercel, and E2B.</p>
<h2 id="computer-use-on-linux-and-mac" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#computer-use-on-linux-and-mac" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Computer use on Linux and Mac</h2>
<p>Self-hosted workers now support computer use on Linux and Mac. With the right desktop packages, an agent can click, type, take screenshots, and drive the browser. You can watch its desktop or take control from Cursor.</p></div></div></div></div></article><article><div class="grid-cursor gap-y-0  mb-v5 "><div class="mb-v2/12 col-span-full max-xl:mx-auto max-xl:w-full max-xl:max-w-[48rem] xl:col-end-7"><p class="text-theme-text-sec sticky top-[var(--site-sticky-top)] left-[-1px] inline-flex items-center"><a class="hover:text-theme-text inline-flex items-center" href="/changelog/start-from-scratch"><time dateTime="2026-08-27T00:00:00.000Z" class="type-base">Aug 27, 2026</time></a><span class="xl:hidden"> · </span><a class="text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text active:text-theme-text xl:hidden" href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="start-from-scratch-without-a-repo"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/start-from-scratch">Start from scratch, without a repo</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>Cloud Agents no longer require a connected GitHub or other third-party SCM provider to get started. Prompt from the get-go, then save your work to a Cursor Origin repo.</p>
<h2 id="get-started" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#get-started" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Get started</h2>
<p>Select <strong>Start from scratch</strong> in the repo picker, then prompt the agent. In the background, Cursor creates an Origin repo for you.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Start from scratch in the repo picker" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fstart-from-scratch-QflXlxizUwAvBbal0Kst46I0mEZT93.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fstart-from-scratch-QflXlxizUwAvBbal0Kst46I0mEZT93.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fstart-from-scratch-QflXlxizUwAvBbal0Kst46I0mEZT93.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="turn-it-into-a-real-repo-whenever-you-want" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#turn-it-into-a-real-repo-whenever-you-want" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Turn it into a real repo, whenever you want</h2>
<p>Once the agent&#x27;s build is to your liking, click the <strong>Create repo</strong> button to save your work in an Origin repo. Choose a custom name or pick one of the suggested ones, then set the visibility to private or internal. You&#x27;ll get a fully scaffolded Origin repo, ready to share or keep building on. Navigate to the Codebase tab to find your repo and access your project.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/yEdl83bhgp2jxRDt2FWFXUEiz4cheJgy64qFPxSqNRI/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h2 id="a-live-preview-right-in-the-browser" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#a-live-preview-right-in-the-browser" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>A live preview, right in the browser</h2>
<p>Cursor now port-forwards your cloud agent&#x27;s live environment straight to your browser, so you can preview it and use tools like design mode.</p>
<h2 id="publish-your-work" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#publish-your-work" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Publish your work</h2>
<p>Connect a Vercel account and hit publish to get a live URL for what you built.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/3oSuYfWwhu5oxtFIWtolOleAS02gGKQX1g00vVR4p02UfE/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>A Vercel account is required to use the publish feature.</p>
<p><a href="https://cursor.com/agents" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Get started today</a>.</p></div></div></div></div></article><div class="grid-cursor"><div class="col-span-full href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="remote-control-for-local-agents"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/remote-control-local-agents">Remote control for local agents</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>You can now see and reply to the local agents running on your computer from the Cursor iOS app.</p>
<h2 id="get-started" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#get-started" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Get started</h2>
<p>Remote Control is on by default for everyone except Enterprise organizations.</p>
<p>Download the Cursor iOS app and sign in. Computers on your account appear in the app automatically. Tap your computer in the app and approve your pairing request in the Cursor desktop app. Your local agents appear in a list. Tap one to see what it&#x27;s doing or send it a message.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Remote Control for local agents in the Cursor iOS app" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fremote-control-cl-pezewO3SZRrIQxMNaTzdpsP9TD1ChS.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fremote-control-cl-pezewO3SZRrIQxMNaTzdpsP9TD1ChS.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fremote-control-cl-pezewO3SZRrIQxMNaTzdpsP9TD1ChS.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="agents-keep-running-on-your-computer" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#agents-keep-running-on-your-computer" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Agents keep running on your computer</h2>
<p>Remote control doesn&#x27;t move your agents anywhere. It keeps running on your computer, and the app connects to it. Your computer needs to stay on and online for remote control to work.</p>
<h2 id="keep-your-computer-awake" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#keep-your-computer-awake" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Keep your computer awake</h2>
<p>To stop your computer from sleeping while you&#x27;re away, turn on &quot;Keep this computer awake&quot; under Remote Control in Cursor&#x27;s desktop settings. Your computer needs to be plugged in with the lid open.</p>
<h2 id="for-enterprise-teams" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#for-enterprise-teams" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>For Enterprise teams</h2>
<p>Remote control is on by default, except for Enterprise organizations. Enterprise admins can turn it on in Org settings &gt; Security and identity &gt; Remote control.</p>
<p>Remote control doesn&#x27;t require cloud agents to work.</p>
<p>Remote control is available today in the <a href="https://cursor.com/mobile" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Cursor iOS app</a>.</p></div></div></div></div></article><article><div class="grid-cursor gap-y-0 pb-v5 mb-v5 border-theme-border-02 border-b"><div class="mb-v2/12 col-span-full max-xl:mx-auto max-xl:w-full max-xl:max-w-[48rem] xl:col-end-7"><p class="text-theme-text-sec sticky top-[var(--site-sticky-top)] left-[-1px] inline-flex items-center"><a class="hover:text-theme-text inline-flex items-center" href="/changelog/rollouts-and-security-reviewer"><time dateTime="2026-09-23T00:00:00.000Z" class="type-base">Sep 23, 2026</time></a><span class="xl:hidden"> · </span><a class="text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text active:text-theme-text xl:hidden" href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="rollouts-and-security-review"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/rollouts-and-security-reviewer">Rollouts and Security Review</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>Today we&#x27;re launching two Cursor bots for the last mile of shipping code. Rollouts watches every change as it deploys and reports its health per environment. Security Review reports exploitable bugs on every pull request.</p>
<p>Both are available today on Teams and Enterprise plans.</p>
<h2 id="rollouts" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#rollouts" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Rollouts</h2>
<p>Rollouts attaches a monitor to every pull request and watches the change as it deploys, reporting change health per environment: verified healthy, regression detected, or inconclusive. It&#x27;s the Cursor version of <a href="https://cursor.com/blog/firetiger" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">Firetiger</a> Change Monitors, rebuilt with the Bot Development Kit.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/5Tb5ctSIPf90200no008q8EIiacgKGmFjxrFLk1tAmRmjI/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>Enable it from the dashboard and connect source control, your deploy system, and your telemetry provider. Rollouts starts watching on the next pull request.</p>
<h4 id="monitoring-plans" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#monitoring-plans" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Monitoring plans</h4>
<p>When a pull request opens, Rollouts reads the diff and the systems it touches, then writes a monitoring plan as a PR comment. The plan lists the risks it identified, the effect the change is meant to have, the signals it will check, and any gaps in instrumentation that would make the change hard to verify. Edit the plan in the PR and Rollouts uses your version.</p>
<h4 id="deploy-tracking" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#deploy-tracking" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Deploy tracking</h4>
<p>Rollouts wakes on deploy events for the change&#x27;s commit and runs the plan against your logs, metrics, and traces. It tracks each environment separately, so a change can be verified in staging and still flagged in production. Rollouts checks the change&#x27;s intended effect alongside error and latency signals, and reports back on the PR when it reaches a verdict.</p>
<h4 id="regressions" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#regressions" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Regressions</h4>
<p>When Rollouts detects a regression, it names the change it suspects and notifies the author. Depending on configuration, it can also open a revert PR for review or hand the finding to a cloud agent for a fix. Rollouts does not merge or roll back on its own today.</p>
<h4 id="integrations" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#integrations" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Integrations</h4>
<p>Rollouts connects to Origin or GitHub for source control, to your continuous delivery system for deploy events, and to Datadog and other telemetry providers for signals. Feature flag integration is coming soon.</p>
<h2 id="security-review" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#security-review" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Security Review</h2>
<p>Security Review is available today. It reads every pull request in the context of the codebase and posts one review comment reporting exploitable bugs. Style and quality stay with Bugbot.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Security Review comment on a pull request reporting an exploitable bug with a severity and proposed fix" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fsecurity-review-N8azgyLevr8FvNIRqJN6hk71os2Oxu.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fsecurity-review-N8azgyLevr8FvNIRqJN6hk71os2Oxu.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fsecurity-review-N8azgyLevr8FvNIRqJN6hk71os2Oxu.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<p>Enable it from the dashboard for the repositories you want reviewed. Draft PRs are skipped.</p>
<h4 id="what-it-reports" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#what-it-reports" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>What it reports</h4>
<p>Security Review looks for injection across SQL, command, and template surfaces, along with authentication and authorization bypasses, including checks that a refactor stopped running. It also flags secrets and credentials committed to source, SSRF and unvalidated redirects, unsafe deserialization, and dependency changes that introduce known vulnerabilities. It traces where user input enters and what it passes through.</p>
<h4 id="findings" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#findings" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Findings</h4>
<p>Each finding carries a severity, the attack path, and a proposed fix. Dismiss one with a reason and Security Review won&#x27;t raise it again on that PR.</p>
<h4 id="team-rules" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#team-rules" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Team rules</h4>
<p>Add rules for your codebase, such as which client external calls must go through or which tables are never queried from a request handler, and Security Review enforces them on every PR.</p>
<h2 id="get-started" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#get-started" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Get started</h2>
<p>Rollouts and Security Reviewer are available today on Teams and Enterprise plans. Enable either bot from the <a href="https://cursor.com/automations" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">automations</a> tab.</p>
<p>For the next 10 days, we&#x27;re including usage credits so teams can try Rollouts on real changes. Teams and Enterprise customers receive credits for roughly 50 and 500 changes, respectively.</p></div></div></div></div></article><article><div class="grid-cursor gap-y-0 pb-v5 mb-v5 border-theme-border-02 border-b"><div class="mb-v2/12 col-span-full max-xl:mx-auto max-xl:w-full max-xl:max-w-[48rem] xl:col-end-7"><p class="text-theme-text-sec sticky top-[var(--site-sticky-top)] left-[-1px] inline-flex items-center"><a class="hover:text-theme-text inline-flex items-center" href="/changelog/projects"><time dateTime="2026-09-10T00:00:00.000Z" class="type-base">Sep 10, 2026</time></a><span class="xl:hidden"> · </span><a class="text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text active:text-theme-text xl:hidden" href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="cursor-projects"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/projects">Cursor Projects</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/7PpKLPBRpzltNUsAM2tITF544siux77yeTAtxXaM5zY/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>Today we&#x27;re launching Projects in Cursor. Projects lets you take on larger bodies of work, such as a feature, a migration, or a full app. It maintains context over months of work, delegates tasks to thousands of subagents, and performs recurring work without being prompted.</p>
<p>Access Projects from the left-hand nav. The coordinator agent in a project doesn&#x27;t write code itself; it plans the work, delegates it to agents that implement it, and brings the finished work back to you to check. Coordinators create and manage agents on your behalf, running as many in parallel as the work needs.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/guK4iheYZylsctjoMBOuaqStvXVcqvHC7KfB022wD9g00/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h2 id="powered-by-cloud-agents" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#powered-by-cloud-agents" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Powered by Cloud Agents</h2>
<p>A Project runs on its own computer in the cloud, so closing your laptop doesn&#x27;t stop it. When something needs testing on your machine, the coordinator spins up a local agent to run it there.</p>
<h2 id="shared-context" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#shared-context" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Shared context</h2>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/pVrq015he7aaw7HqmbsMMYrOMMVmhkOZQn01hqLBhHqSE/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>You shouldn&#x27;t have to onboard an agent every time you start a task. Each Project maintains a set of files that sync across every cloud and local machine its agents use. Agents add research and artifacts, along with what they learn about the codebase and how you prefer work to be done. If one agent figures out how to test a service, for example, every future agent can use those instructions. The shared context grows with the Project, making the coordinator more effective over time.</p>
<h2 id="subscriptions" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#subscriptions" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Subscriptions</h2>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/F02pXSeJF6CAeEE39x6AM6EHptkXadTzcHwoJ8yNd88o/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<p>Tell the coordinator agent to watch a Slack channel, run on a schedule, or follow all your PRs. This way it can take action based on signals it detects, without waiting for your prompt.</p>
<p>Connect Slack and point it at a bug-report channel, and it starts delegating each time a bug comes in.</p>
<p>Projects are available in beta and rolling out to all users starting today.</p></div></div></div></div></article><article><div class="grid-cursor gap-y-0 pb-v5 mb-v5 border-theme-border-02 border-b"><div class="mb-v2/12 col-span-full max-xl:mx-auto max-xl:w-full max-xl:max-w-[48rem] xl:col-end-7"><p class="text-theme-text-sec sticky top-[var(--site-sticky-top)] left-[-1px] inline-flex items-center"><a class="hover:text-theme-text inline-flex items-center" href="/changelog/self-hosted-machines"><time dateTime="2026-09-02T00:00:00.000Z" class="type-base">Sep 2, 2026</time></a><span class="xl:hidden"> · </span><a class="text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text active:text-theme-text xl:hidden" href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="self-hosted-machines"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/self-hosted-machines">Self-hosted machines</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>Cursor supports <strong>self-hosted machines</strong>, which let you keep tool execution entirely in your own network.</p>
<p>Your codebase, build outputs, and secrets all stay on internal machines running in your infrastructure, while the agent handles tool calls locally.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Run on menu showing Remote Machines with self-hosted options lambda-test, cloud-demo, and jacks-desktop" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fremote-machines-QjJ0ZzGDelSdT7v2CXDdh0BQHqjmH0.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fremote-machines-QjJ0ZzGDelSdT7v2CXDdh0BQHqjmH0.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fremote-machines-QjJ0ZzGDelSdT7v2CXDdh0BQHqjmH0.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="dynamic-pool-scheduling" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#dynamic-pool-scheduling" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Dynamic pool scheduling</h2>
<p><strong>My Machines</strong> connects a single laptop or VM to your account for personal workflows.</p>
<p><strong>Team pools</strong> are named queues of workers for a team or enterprise. Capacity can grow as requests arrive and shrink when workers disconnect, so your self-hosted machines can scale with demand. Pools are not tied to one repository: name the pool, and any available worker can claim the request.</p>
<p>Pools can also hibernate idle machines, then restore within a reconnect window when a follow-up arrives, so you don&#x27;t keep expensive capacity warm just for the next prompt.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Cloud Agents dashboard listing Self-hosted Machines pools with active and idle worker counts" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fpools-mNNea8rJyNxaBuz7rSVT2SJOKkRsmv.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fpools-mNNea8rJyNxaBuz7rSVT2SJOKkRsmv.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fuploads%2Fpools-mNNea8rJyNxaBuz7rSVT2SJOKkRsmv.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="run-on-your-sandboxes" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#run-on-your-sandboxes" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Run on your sandboxes</h2>
<p>Cloud agents can now execute on <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/cloud-agent/self-hosted/integrations" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">infrastructure you already use</a>, including from AWS Lambda, Coder, Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, Namespace, Vercel, and E2B.</p>
<h2 id="computer-use-on-linux-and-mac" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#computer-use-on-linux-and-mac" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Computer use on Linux and Mac</h2>
<p>Self-hosted workers now support computer use on Linux and Mac. With the right desktop packages, an agent can click, type, take screenshots, and drive the browser. You can watch its desktop or take control from Cursor.</p></div></div></div></div></article><article><div class="grid-cursor gap-y-0  mb-v5 "><div class="mb-v2/12 col-span-full max-xl:mx-auto max-xl:w-full max-xl:max-w-[48rem] xl:col-end-7"><p class="text-theme-text-sec sticky top-[var(--site-sticky-top)] left-[-1px] inline-flex items-center"><a class="hover:text-theme-text inline-flex items-center" href="/changelog/start-from-scratch"><time dateTime="2026-08-27T00:00:00.000Z" class="type-base">Aug 27, 2026</time></a><span class="xl:hidden"> · </span><a class="text-theme-text-sec hover:text-theme-text active:text-theme-text xl:hidden" href="/changelog">Changelog</a></p></div><div class="col-span-full xl:col-start-7 xl:col-end-19"><div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-[48rem]"><header class="mb-v1 relative"><h1 class="type-lg text-balance" id="start-from-scratch-without-a-repo"><a class="active:text-theme-text hover:opacity-90" href="/changelog/start-from-scratch">Start from scratch, without a repo</a></h1></header><div class="prose prose--block"><p>Cloud Agents no longer require a connected GitHub or other third-party SCM provider to get started. Prompt from the get-go, then save your work to a Cursor Origin repo.</p>
<h2 id="get-started" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#get-started" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Get started</h2>
<p>Select <strong>Start from scratch</strong> in the repo picker, then prompt the agent. In the background, Cursor creates an Origin repo for you.</p>
<figure><div class="media-border-container overflow-hidden"><img alt="Start from scratch in the repo picker" loading="lazy" width="800" height="450" decoding="async" data-nimg="1" class="transition-opacity duration-[220ms] ease-[var(--ease-out-spring)] will-change-[opacity] opacity-0" style="color:transparent" srcSet="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fstart-from-scratch-QflXlxizUwAvBbal0Kst46I0mEZT93.png&amp;w=828&amp;q=70 1x, /marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fstart-from-scratch-QflXlxizUwAvBbal0Kst46I0mEZT93.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70 2x" src="/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fchangelog%2Fstart-from-scratch-QflXlxizUwAvBbal0Kst46I0mEZT93.png&amp;w=1920&amp;q=70"/></div></figure>
<h2 id="turn-it-into-a-real-repo-whenever-you-want" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#turn-it-into-a-real-repo-whenever-you-want" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Turn it into a real repo, whenever you want</h2>
<p>Once the agent&#x27;s build is to your liking, click the <strong>Create repo</strong> button to save your work in an Origin repo. Choose a custom name or pick one of the suggested ones, then set the visibility to private or internal. You&#x27;ll get a fully scaffolded Origin repo, ready to share or keep building on. Navigate to the Codebase tab to find your repo and access your project.</p>
<figure class="!my-1"><div style="overflow:hidden;width:fit-content;max-width:100%"><div class="media-border-container media-controller  " style="aspect-ratio:16/9;max-width:100%;width:100%;background-color:var(--theme-bg-sec, #1a1a1a);background-image:url(https://image.mux.com/yEdl83bhgp2jxRDt2FWFXUEiz4cheJgy64qFPxSqNRI/thumbnail.jpg?time=0);background-size:cover;background-position:center"></div></div></figure>
<h2 id="a-live-preview-right-in-the-browser" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#a-live-preview-right-in-the-browser" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>A live preview, right in the browser</h2>
